latin: Suave, mari magno turbantibus aequora ventis
en: Sweet it is, when on the great sea the winds are churning the waters,

latin: e terra magnum alterius spectare laborem;
en: to watch from land the great toil of another;

latin: non quia vexari quemquamst iucunda voluptas,
en: not because anyone's distress is a delightful pleasure,

latin: sed quibus ipse malis careas quia cernere suavest.
en: but because it is sweet to see what evils you yourself are free of.

latin: suave etiam belli certamina magna tueri
en: Sweet, too, to look upon the great contests of war

latin: per campos instructa tua sine parte pericli;
en: drawn up across the plains, with no share of your own in the danger;

latin: sed nihil dulcius est, bene quam munita tenere
en: but nothing is sweeter than to hold the well-fortified

latin: edita doctrina sapientum templa serena,
en: serene precincts, set on high by the teaching of the wise,

latin: despicere unde queas alios passimque videre
en: from where you can look down on others and see them everywhere

latin: errare atque viam palantis quaerere vitae,
en: wandering and, straying here and there, seeking the road of life,

latin: certare ingenio, contendere nobilitate,
en: contending in talent, competing in nobility of birth,

latin: noctes atque dies niti praestante labore
en: striving night and day with surpassing labor

latin: ad summas emergere opes rerumque potiri.
en: to rise to the height of wealth and gain the mastery of things.

latin: o miseras hominum mentes, o pectora caeca!
en: O miserable minds of men, O blind hearts!

latin: qualibus in tenebris vitae quantisque periclis
en: In what darkness of life and in how great dangers

latin: degitur hoc aevi quod cumquest! nonne videre
en: this span of life, whatever it is, is passed! Do you not see

latin: nihil aliud sibi naturam latrare, nisi ut qui
en: that nature barks for nothing else for herself than this, that

latin: corpore seiunctus dolor absit, mente fruatur
en: pain be parted from the body and be absent, and the mind enjoy

latin: iucundo sensu cura semota metuque?
en: a pleasant feeling, set apart from care and fear?

latin: ergo corpoream ad naturam pauca videmus
en: Therefore we see that for the body's nature few things

latin: esse opus omnino: quae demant cumque dolorem,
en: are needed at all: such things as take away pain,

latin: delicias quoque uti multas substernere possint
en: and such that they can also spread out many delights for us,

latin: gratius inter dum, neque natura ipsa requirit,
en: more welcome now and then; nor does nature herself feel the want,

latin: si non aurea sunt iuvenum simulacra per aedes
en: if there are no golden images of youths about the halls

latin: lampadas igniferas manibus retinentia dextris,
en: holding fire-bearing lamps in their right hands

latin: lumina nocturnis epulis ut suppeditentur,
en: so that light may be supplied for feasts by night,

latin: nec domus argento fulget auroque renidet
en: nor the house gleam with silver and shine with gold,

latin: nec citharae reboant laqueata aurataque templa,
en: nor lyres echo through paneled and gilded rafters,

latin: cum tamen inter se prostrati in gramine molli
en: when still, lying together on the soft grass

latin: propter aquae rivum sub ramis arboris altae
en: beside a stream of water under the boughs of a tall tree,

latin: non magnis opibus iucunde corpora curant,
en: with no great wealth they tend their bodies pleasantly,

latin: praesertim cum tempestas adridet et anni
en: above all when the weather smiles and the seasons

latin: tempora conspergunt viridantis floribus herbas.
en: of the year sprinkle the greening grass with flowers.

latin: nec calidae citius decedunt corpore febres,
en: Nor do hot fevers leave the body any faster

latin: textilibus si in picturis ostroque rubenti
en: if you are tossed on woven pictures and blushing purple

latin: iacteris, quam si in plebeia veste cubandum est.
en: than if you must lie beneath a common man's coverlet.

latin: quapropter quoniam nihil nostro in corpore gazae
en: Therefore, since in our body treasures are of no profit,

latin: proficiunt neque nobilitas nec gloria regni,
en: nor nobility, nor the glory of a kingdom,

latin: quod super est, animo quoque nil prodesse putandum;
en: for the rest, we must think they do the mind no good either;

latin: si non forte tuas legiones per loca campi
en: unless perhaps, when you see your legions across the Campus

latin: fervere cum videas belli simulacra cientis,
en: seething as they stir up the images of war,

latin: subsidiis magnis et opum vi constabilitas,
en: made firm with great reserves and a force of wealth,

latin: ornatas armis stlattas pariterque animatas,
en: your ships fitted out with arms, all alike full of spirit,

latin: his tibi tum rebus timefactae religiones
en: then, before these things, the religions in their terror

latin: effugiunt animo pavidae mortisque timores
en: flee panic-stricken from your mind, and the fears of death

latin: tum vacuum pectus lincunt curaque solutum.
en: then leave your heart empty and loosed from care.

latin: quod si ridicula haec ludibriaque esse videmus,
en: But if we see that these things are laughable and a mockery,

latin: re veraque metus hominum curaeque sequaces
en: and in truth the fears of men and the cares that dog them

latin: nec metuunt sonitus armorum nec fera tela
en: fear neither the clash of arms nor savage weapons,

latin: audacterque inter reges rerumque potentis
en: and boldly move among kings and the masters of things,

latin: versantur neque fulgorem reverentur ab auro
en: and do not stand in awe of the glitter that comes from gold

latin: nec clarum vestis splendorem purpureai,
en: nor the bright splendor of a purple robe,

latin: quid dubitas quin omnis sit haec rationis potestas,
en: why do you doubt that this power belongs wholly to reasoning,

latin: omnis cum in tenebris praesertim vita laboret?
en: especially when all life labors in darkness?

latin: nam vel uti pueri trepidant atque omnia caecis
en: For just as children tremble and fear everything

latin: in tenebris metuunt, sic nos in luce timemus
en: in blind darkness, so we in the light are afraid

latin: inter dum, nihilo quae sunt metuenda magis quam
en: at times of things that are no more to be feared than

latin: quae pueri in tenebris pavitant finguntque futura.
en: what children in the dark shudder at and imagine will come.

latin: hunc igitur terrorem animi tenebrasque necessest
en: This terror of the mind, then, and this darkness

latin: non radii solis neque lucida tela diei
en: must be scattered not by the sun's rays or the bright shafts of day

latin: discutiant, sed naturae species ratioque.
en: but by the face and reasoning of nature.

latin: Nunc age, quo motu genitalia materiai
en: Come now, by what motion the generative bodies of matter

latin: corpora res varias gignant genitasque resolvant
en: beget the various things and dissolve them once begotten,

latin: et qua vi facere id cogantur quaeque sit ollis
en: and by what force they are compelled to do it, and what

latin: reddita mobilitas magnum per inane meandi,
en: mobility is given them for travelling through the great void,

latin: expediam: tu te dictis praebere memento.
en: I shall explain; you, remember to give yourself to my words.

latin: nam certe non inter se stipata cohaeret
en: For certainly matter does not cling together, packed close

latin: materies, quoniam minui rem quamque videmus
en: in a mass, since we see each thing diminish,

latin: et quasi longinquo fluere omnia cernimus aevo
en: and we perceive all things flowing away, as it were, over long age,

latin: ex oculisque vetustatem subducere nostris,
en: and age withdrawing them from our eyes,

latin: cum tamen incolumis videatur summa manere
en: while yet the sum is seen to remain unimpaired,

latin: propterea quia, quae decedunt corpora cuique,
en: because the bodies that depart from each thing

latin: unde abeunt minuunt, quo venere augmine donant.
en: diminish what they leave, and on what they come to bestow increase.

latin: illa senescere, at haec contra florescere cogunt,
en: They force the one to grow old and the other in turn to flower,

latin: nec remorantur ibi. sic rerum summa novatur
en: and do not linger there. So the sum of things is ever

latin: semper, et inter se mortales mutua vivunt.
en: renewed, and mortals live by exchange among themselves.

latin: augescunt aliae gentes, aliae minuuntur,
en: Some races increase, others are diminished,

latin: inque brevi spatio mutantur saecla animantum
en: and in a brief space the generations of living things are changed

latin: et quasi cursores vitai lampada tradunt.
en: and like runners pass on the torch of life.

latin: Si cessare putas rerum primordia posse
en: If you think the first-beginnings of things can stand still

latin: cessandoque novos rerum progignere motus,
en: and by standing still beget new motions of things,

latin: avius a vera longe ratione vagaris.
en: you wander far astray from true reasoning.

latin: nam quoniam per inane vagantur, cuncta necessest
en: For since they wander through the void, all the first-beginnings

latin: aut gravitate sua ferri primordia rerum
en: of things must be carried either by their own weight

latin: aut ictu forte alterius. nam cum cita saepe
en: or perhaps by the blow of another. For when, swift, they have often

latin: obvia conflixere, fit ut diversa repente
en: met and clashed, it comes about that suddenly they spring

latin: dissiliant; neque enim mirum, durissima quae sint
en: apart in different ways; and no wonder, since they are very hard,

latin: ponderibus solidis neque quicquam a tergibus obstet.
en: solid in their weight, and nothing blocks them from behind.

latin: et quo iactari magis omnia materiai
en: And so that you may see more clearly that all the bodies

latin: corpora pervideas, reminiscere totius imum
en: of matter are tossed about, remember that the whole

latin: nil esse in summa, neque habere ubi corpora prima
en: has no bottom in the sum, and the first bodies have no place

latin: consistant, quoniam spatium sine fine modoquest
en: to come to rest, since space is without end or limit,

latin: inmensumque patere in cunctas undique partis
en: and spreads immeasurable in all directions everywhere

latin: pluribus ostendi et certa ratione probatumst.
en: as I have shown in many words and proved by sure reasoning.

latin: quod quoniam constat, ni mirum nulla quies est
en: And since this is settled, surely no rest

latin: reddita corporibus primis per inane profundum,
en: is given to the first bodies through the deep void,

latin: sed magis adsiduo varioque exercita motu
en: but rather, driven by unceasing and varied motion,

latin: partim intervallis magnis confulta resultant,
en: some, when they have collided, leap back over great intervals,

latin: pars etiam brevibus spatiis vexantur ab ictu.
en: and some are harried by the blow within short spaces.

latin: et quae cumque magis condenso conciliatu
en: And all those that, in a denser union,

latin: exiguis intervallis convecta resultant,
en: brought together, rebound across small intervals,

latin: indupedita suis perplexis ipsa figuris,
en: entangled by their own interlocking shapes,

latin: haec validas saxi radices et fera ferri
en: these form the strong roots of rock and the savage bodies

latin: corpora constituunt et cetera de genere horum.
en: of iron, and the other things of this kind.

latin: paucula quae porro magnum per inane vagantur,
en: Those few others that wander on through the great void

latin: cetera dissiliunt longe longeque recursant
en: leap far apart and run far back again

latin: in magnis intervallis; haec aera rarum
en: across great intervals; these furnish us the thin air

latin: sufficiunt nobis et splendida lumina solis.
en: and the shining light of the sun.

latin: multaque praeterea magnum per inane vagantur,
en: And many besides wander through the great void

latin: conciliis rerum quae sunt reiecta nec usquam
en: which have been thrown out of the unions of things and nowhere

latin: consociare etiam motus potuere recepta.
en: have been able, even when let in, to join their motions together.

latin: Cuius, uti memoro, rei simulacrum et imago
en: Of this thing, as I tell, an image and picture

latin: ante oculos semper nobis versatur et instat.
en: is always turning before our eyes and pressing on us.

latin: contemplator enim, cum solis lumina cumque
en: For look closely, whenever the sun's light is poured

latin: inserti fundunt radii per opaca domorum:
en: by rays let in through the darkened places of houses:

latin: multa minuta modis multis per inane videbis
en: you will see many minute bodies in many ways, through the void,

latin: corpora misceri radiorum lumine in ipso
en: mingling in the very light of the rays,

latin: et vel ut aeterno certamine proelia pugnas
en: and as though in everlasting conflict waging wars and battles,

latin: edere turmatim certantia nec dare pausam,
en: fighting troop by troop, and giving no pause,

latin: conciliis et discidiis exercita crebris;
en: driven on by frequent unions and partings;

latin: conicere ut possis ex hoc, primordia rerum
en: so that from this you may guess what it is for the first-beginnings

latin: quale sit in magno iactari semper inani.
en: of things to be tossed forever in the great void.

latin: dum taxat, rerum magnarum parva potest res
en: So far as it goes, a small thing can give

latin: exemplare dare et vestigia notitiai.
en: a pattern of great things and the tracks of knowledge.

latin: Hoc etiam magis haec animum te advertere par est
en: For this reason, too, it is more fitting that you attend to these

latin: corpora quae in solis radiis turbare videntur,
en: bodies that are seen to be in turmoil in the sun's rays,

latin: quod tales turbae motus quoque materiai
en: because such turmoils signify that there are motions

latin: significant clandestinos caecosque subesse.
en: of matter, too, hidden and blind, beneath them.

latin: multa videbis enim plagis ibi percita caecis
en: For you will see many there, struck by blind blows,

latin: commutare viam retroque repulsa reverti
en: change their course and, driven back, return,

latin: nunc huc nunc illuc in cunctas undique partis.
en: now this way, now that, in all directions everywhere.

latin: scilicet hic a principiis est omnibus error.
en: This wandering, you may be sure, all comes from the beginnings.

latin: prima moventur enim per se primordia rerum,
en: For first the first-beginnings of things move of themselves;

latin: inde ea quae parvo sunt corpora conciliatu
en: then those bodies that are formed of a small union

latin: et quasi proxima sunt ad viris principiorum,
en: and are, as it were, nearest to the strength of the beginnings

latin: ictibus illorum caecis inpulsa cientur,
en: are set going, struck by their blind blows,

latin: ipsaque proporro paulo maiora lacessunt.
en: and they in turn assail bodies a little larger.

latin: sic a principiis ascendit motus et exit
en: So motion rises from the beginnings and comes out

latin: paulatim nostros ad sensus, ut moveantur
en: little by little to our senses, so that those too

latin: illa quoque, in solis quae lumine cernere quimus
en: are moved which we can make out in the light of the sun,

latin: nec quibus id faciant plagis apparet aperte.
en: though by what blows they do it does not plainly appear.

latin: Nunc quae mobilitas sit reddita materiai
en: Now what mobility has been given to the bodies

latin: corporibus, paucis licet hinc cognoscere, Memmi.
en: of matter, Memmius, you may learn from this in a few words.

latin: primum aurora novo cum spargit lumine terras
en: First, when dawn sprinkles the lands with new light,

latin: et variae volucres nemora avia pervolitantes
en: and the many-colored birds, flitting through the pathless woods,

latin: aera per tenerum liquidis loca vocibus opplent,
en: fill the places through the soft air with liquid voices,

latin: quam subito soleat sol ortus tempore tali
en: how suddenly the sun, once risen, is used at such a time

latin: convestire sua perfundens omnia luce,
en: to clothe all things, flooding them with his light,

latin: omnibus in promptu manifestumque esse videmus.
en: we see to be ready to hand and plain for all.

latin: at vapor is, quem sol mittit, lumenque serenum
en: But that heat which the sun sends out, and its calm light,

latin: non per inane meat vacuum; quo tardius ire
en: does not travel through empty void; and so it is forced

latin: cogitur, aerias quasi dum diverberat undas;
en: to go more slowly, as it beats its way, as it were, through waves of air;

latin: nec singillatim corpuscula quaeque vaporis
en: nor do the little bodies of heat travel one by one,

latin: sed complexa meant inter se conque globata;
en: but tangled with one another and massed together;

latin: qua propter simul inter se retrahuntur et extra
en: and so at once they are dragged back by one another and hindered

latin: officiuntur, uti cogantur tardius ire.
en: from outside, so that they are forced to go more slowly.

latin: at quae sunt solida primordia simplicitate,
en: But the first-beginnings that are of solid singleness,

latin: cum per inane meant vacuum nec res remoratur
en: when they travel through empty void and nothing delays them

latin: ulla foris atque ipsa suis e partibus unum,
en: from outside, and they themselves, one whole from their own parts,

latin: unum, in quem coepere, locum conixa feruntur,
en: are borne, straining, toward the one place they began to move to,

latin: debent ni mirum praecellere mobilitate
en: must surely surpass in mobility

latin: et multo citius ferri quam lumina solis
en: and be carried far more swiftly than the light of the sun,

latin: multiplexque loci spatium transcurrere eodem
en: and run through many times the extent of space in the same

latin: tempore quo solis pervolgant fulgura caelum.
en: time in which the sun's flashes spread through heaven.

latin: nec persectari primordia singula quaeque,
en: nor to follow out each single first-beginning,

latin: ut videant qua quicque geratur cum ratione.
en: to see by what principle each thing comes about.

latin: At quidam contra haec, ignari materiai,
en: But some, against this, ignorant of matter,

latin: naturam non posse deum sine numine reddunt
en: hold that nature cannot, without the power of the gods,

latin: tanto opere humanis rationibus atmoderate
en: so closely fitted, in such measure, to human needs,

latin: tempora mutare annorum frugesque creare
en: change the seasons of the years and create the crops

latin: et iam cetera, mortalis quae suadet adire
en: and all the other things that mortals are urged to approach,

latin: ipsaque deducit dux vitae dia voluptas
en: and to which divine pleasure herself, the guide of life, leads them,

latin: et res per Veneris blanditur saecla propagent,
en: coaxing them through the works of Venus to propagate their generations,

latin: ne genus occidat humanum. quorum omnia causa
en: so that the human race should not perish. When they imagine

latin: constituisse deos cum fingunt, omnibus rebus
en: the gods have ordered all things for men's sake, in every way

latin: magno opere a vera lapsi ratione videntur.
en: they seem to have slipped greatly from true reasoning.

latin: nam quamvis rerum ignorem primordia quae sint,
en: For even if I did not know what the first-beginnings of things are,

latin: hoc tamen ex ipsis caeli rationibus ausim
en: this, still, from the very order of heaven I would dare

latin: confirmare aliisque ex rebus reddere multis,
en: to affirm, and to show from many other things,

latin: nequaquam nobis divinitus esse creatam
en: that by no means for us, by divine power, was created

latin: naturam mundi: tanta stat praedita culpa.
en: the nature of the world: so great the flaws it stands endowed with.

latin: quae tibi posterius, Memmi, faciemus aperta;
en: These things, Memmius, I will make plain to you later;

latin: nunc id quod super est de motibus expediemus.
en: now I will set out what remains concerning motions.

latin: Nunc locus est, ut opinor, in his illud quoque rebus
en: Now is the place, I think, in these matters to prove this too

latin: confirmare tibi, nullam rem posse sua vi
en: to you: that no bodily thing can by its own force

latin: corpoream sursum ferri sursumque meare.
en: be carried upward and travel upward.

latin: ne tibi dent in eo flammarum corpora frudem;
en: Do not let the bodies of flames deceive you in this;

latin: sursus enim versus gignuntur et augmina sumunt
en: for they are born upward and take on their increase,

latin: et sursum nitidae fruges arbustaque crescunt,
en: and upward the shining crops and the trees grow,

latin: pondera, quantum in se est, cum deorsum cuncta ferantur.
en: though all weights, as far as in them lies, are carried downward.

latin: nec cum subsiliunt ignes ad tecta domorum
en: Nor, when fires leap up to the roofs of houses

latin: et celeri flamma degustant tigna trabesque,
en: and with swift flame lick the rafters and beams,

latin: sponte sua facere id sine vi subiecta putandum est.
en: must we think they do this of themselves, with no force thrust beneath.

latin: quod genus e nostro com missus corpore sanguis
en: Just so the blood let out from our body

latin: emicat exultans alte spargitque cruorem.
en: spurts leaping on high and scatters gore.

latin: nonne vides etiam quanta vi tigna trabesque
en: Do you not see, too, with what force the water's moisture

latin: respuat umor aquae? nam quo magis ursimus altum
en: spits out rafters and beams? For the more we have pushed them deep,

latin: derecta et magna vi multi pressimus aegre,
en: straight down, and many with great force have pressed them, straining,

latin: tam cupide sursum removet magis atque remittit,
en: the more eagerly it thrusts them back up and sends them out,

latin: plus ut parte foras emergant exiliantque.
en: so that they rise and leap out by more than half their length.

latin: nec tamen haec, quantum est in se, dubitamus, opinor,
en: And yet we do not doubt, I think, that these, as far as in them lies,

latin: quin vacuum per inane deorsum cuncta ferantur.
en: are all carried downward through the empty void.

latin: sic igitur debent flammae quoque posse per auras
en: So in the same way flames too must be able, through the breezes

latin: aeris expressae sursum succedere, quamquam
en: of air, squeezed out, to climb upward, although

latin: pondera, quantum in se est, deorsum deducere pugnent.
en: their weights, as far as in them lies, fight to draw them down.

latin: nocturnasque faces caeli sublime volantis
en: And the night torches of heaven, flying aloft,

latin: nonne vides longos flammarum ducere tractus
en: do you not see them draw long trails of flame

latin: in quas cumque dedit partis natura meatum?
en: toward whatever quarter nature has given them passage?

latin: non cadere in terras stellas et sidera cernis?
en: Do you not see stars and constellations falling to the earth?

latin: sol etiam caeli de vertice dissipat omnis
en: The sun also from the summit of heaven scatters its heat

latin: ardorem in partis et lumine conserit arva;
en: to every side and sows the fields with light;

latin: in terras igitur quoque solis vergitur ardor.
en: to the earth, therefore, the sun's heat also tends.

latin: transversosque volare per imbris fulmina cernis,
en: And you see thunderbolts fly slantwise through the rains;

latin: nunc hinc nunc illinc abrupti nubibus ignes
en: now from here, now from there, fires broken from the clouds

latin: concursant; cadit in terras vis flammea volgo.
en: rush together; the flaming force falls everywhere upon the earth.

latin: Illud in his quoque te rebus cognoscere avemus,
en: This too, in these matters, we long for you to know:

latin: corpora cum deorsum rectum per inane feruntur
en: that when bodies are carried straight down through the void

latin: ponderibus propriis, incerto tempore ferme
en: by their own weights, at quite uncertain times

latin: incertisque locis spatio depellere paulum,
en: and uncertain places they push off a little from their course,

latin: tantum quod momen mutatum dicere possis.
en: just so much that you could call it a change of motion.

latin: quod nisi declinare solerent, omnia deorsum
en: For if they were not used to swerve, all things would fall

latin: imbris uti guttae caderent per inane profundum
en: downward like drops of rain through the deep void,

latin: nec foret offensus natus nec plaga creata
en: and no collision would arise, no blow be created

latin: principiis; ita nihil umquam natura creasset.
en: for the beginnings; so nature would never have created anything.

latin: Quod si forte aliquis credit graviora potesse
en: But if perhaps someone believes that heavier bodies,

latin: corpora, quo citius rectum per inane feruntur,
en: because they are carried more swiftly straight through the void,

latin: incidere ex supero levioribus atque ita plagas
en: can fall from above upon the lighter, and so beget

latin: gignere, quae possint genitalis reddere motus,
en: blows that could give rise to generative motions,

latin: avius a vera longe ratione recedit.
en: he strays far away, off the road, from true reasoning.

latin: nam per aquas quae cumque cadunt atque aera rarum,
en: For whatever falls through water and thin air,

latin: haec pro ponderibus casus celerare necessest
en: these must quicken their fall in proportion to their weights,

latin: propterea quia corpus aquae naturaque tenvis
en: because the body of water and the thin nature

latin: aeris haud possunt aeque rem quamque morari,

latin: omnis enim totum per corpus materiai

latin: copia conciri debet, concita per artus

latin: omnis ut studium mentis conixa sequatur;

latin: ut videas initum motus a corde creari

latin: perspicuumst nobis invitis ire rapique,

latin: donec eam refrenavit per membra voluntas.

latin: iamne vides igitur, quamquam vis extera multos

latin: quare in seminibus quoque idem fateare necessest,

latin: esse aliam praeter plagas et pondera causam

latin: de nihilo quoniam fieri nihil posse videmus.

latin: pondus enim prohibet ne plagis omnia fiant

latin: et devicta quasi cogatur ferre patique,

latin: Nec stipata magis fuit umquam materiai

latin: nam neque adaugescit quicquam neque deperit inde.

latin: qua propter quo nunc in motu principiorum

latin: nec rerum summam commutare ulla potest vis;

latin: Illud in his rebus non est mirabile, quare,
en: In these matters it is no wonder why,

latin: omnia cum rerum primordia sint in motu,

latin: praesertim cum, quae possimus cernere, celent

latin: saepe tamen motus spatio diducta locorum.

latin: nam saepe in colli tondentes pabula laeta

latin: invitant herbae gemmantes rore recenti,

latin: et satiati agni ludunt blandeque coruscant;

latin: omnia quae nobis longe confusa videntur

latin: et velut in viridi candor consistere colli.

latin: praeterea magnae legiones cum loca cursu

latin: camporum complent belli simulacra cientes,

latin: aere renidescit tellus supterque virum vi

latin: excitur pedibus sonitus clamoreque montes

latin: et circum volitant equites mediosque repente

latin: et tamen est quidam locus altis montibus, unde

en: Come now, next learn of what sort the origins

latin: non quo multa parum simili sint praedita forma,

latin: sed quia non volgo paria omnibus omnia constant.
en: but because, as a rule, not all are alike to all.

latin: nec mirum; nam cum sit eorum copia tanta,
en: Nor is it a wonder; for since their store is so great

latin: et variae volucres, laetantia quae loca aquarum

latin: quare etiam atque etiam simili ratione necessest,

latin: Huc accedit uti mellis lactisque liquores
en: Add to this that the liquids of honey and of milk

latin: mobilibus digitis expergefacta figurant;

latin: neu simili penetrare putes primordia forma

latin: at contra quae cumque molesta atque aspera constat,

latin: Sunt etiam quae iam nec levia iure putantur

latin: fecula iam quo de genere est inulaeque sapores.

latin: illa quidem debent e levibus atque rutundis

latin: sensibus dentatum, facile ut cognoscere possis

en: is made not of tangled but of sharp elements.

latin: sed quod amara vides eadem quae fluvida constant,
en: But that you see the same things bitter that are fluid,

latin: sudor uti maris est, minime mirabile debet
en: as the sweat of the sea is, ought to be no wonder at all

latin: nam quod fluvidus est, e levibus atque rotundis
en: For because it is fluid, it is made of smooth and round bodies,

latin: est, sed levibus sunt hamata admixta doloris
en: but mixed in with the smooth are hooked

latin: corpora. nec tamen haec retineri hamata necessust:
en: bodies of pain. Yet these hooked ones need not be held fast:

latin: scilicet esse globosa tamen, cum squalida constent,
en: clearly they are round nonetheless, rough though they are,

latin: provolvi simul ut possint et laedere sensus.
en: so that they can at once roll forward and hurt the senses.

latin: et quo mixta putes magis aspera levibus esse
en: And that you may believe the more that rough are mixed with smooth

latin: principiis, unde est Neptuni corpus acerbum,
en: beginnings, from which the body of Neptune gets its bitterness,

latin: est ratio secernendi seorsumque videndi,
en: there is a way of separating them and seeing them apart:

latin: umor dulcis ubi per terras crebrius idem
en: the moisture grows sweet when, through the earth, the same moisture

latin: percolatur, ut in foveam fluat ac mansuescat;
en: is filtered through many times, to flow into a pit and grow mild;

latin: linquit enim supera taetri primordia viri,
en: for it leaves behind, above, the first-beginnings of the foul brine,

latin: aspera quo magis in terris haerescere possint.
en: since, being rough, they can cling the more within the earth.

latin: Quod quoniam docui, pergam conectere rem quae
en: Since I have taught this, I will go on to join to it a fact

latin: ex hoc apta fidem ducat, primordia rerum
en: which, fitted to this, draws its credit: that the first-beginnings of things

latin: finita variare figurarum ratione.
en: vary within a finite range of shapes.

latin: quod si non ita sit, rursum iam semina quaedam
en: For if it were not so, then again certain seeds

latin: esse infinito debebunt corporis auctu.
en: will have to be infinite in the growth of their bodies.

latin: namque in eadem una cuiusvis iam brevitate
en: For within the one same smallness of any given

latin: corporis inter se multum variare figurae
en: body, for the shapes to vary much from one another

latin: non possunt. fac enim minimis e partibus esse
en: is not possible. For suppose that of least parts, three of them,

latin: corpora prima tribus, vel paulo pluribus auge;
en: the first bodies are made, or add a few more to these;

latin: nempe ubi eas partis unius corporis omnis,
en: surely, when all those parts of a single body

latin: summa atque ima locans, transmutans dextera laevis,
en: you have set at top and bottom, and changed the right for the left,

latin: omnimodis expertus eris, quam quisque det ordo
en: and tried in every way what appearance each order gives

latin: formai speciem totius corporis eius,
en: of form to the whole of that body,

latin: quod super est, si forte voles variare figuras,
en: for the rest, if you chance to want to vary the shapes,

latin: addendum partis alias erit. inde sequetur,
en: other parts will have to be added. From this it will follow

latin: adsimili ratione alias ut postulet ordo,
en: that, on a like principle, the order will call for others,

latin: si tu forte voles etiam variare figuras.
en: if you chance to want to vary the shapes still further.

latin: ergo formarum novitatem corporis augmen
en: Therefore growth of body follows upon newness of forms

latin: subsequitur. quare non est ut credere possis
en: close behind. And so there is no way you can believe

latin: esse infinitis distantia semina formis,
en: that seeds exist distinguished by infinite forms,

latin: ne quaedam cogas inmani maximitate
en: lest you force certain of them to be of monstrous greatness,

latin: esse, supra quod iam docui non posse probari.
en: which I have already shown above cannot be proved.

latin: iam tibi barbaricae vestes Meliboeaque fulgens
en: Then barbarian robes and the gleaming Meliboean purple,

latin: purpura Thessalico concharum tacta colore,
en: dipped in the Thessalian color of the shells,

latin: aurea pavonum ridenti imbuta lepore
en: the golden race of peacocks, steeped in laughing charm,

latin: saecla novo rerum superata colore iacerent
en: would lie outdone by some new color in things,

latin: et contemptus odor smyrnae mellisque sapores,
en: and the smell of myrrh would be scorned, and the savors of honey,

latin: et cycnea mele Phoebeaque daedala chordis
en: and the swan's notes and the intricate strains of Phoebus' strings

latin: carmina consimili ratione oppressa silerent;
en: would fall silent, overpowered in like manner;

latin: namque aliis aliud praestantius exoreretur.
en: for one thing would always rise more excellent than another.

latin: cedere item retro possent in deteriores
en: So too all things could fall back toward the worse,

latin: omnia sic partis, ut diximus in melioris;
en: just as we have said they could toward the better;

latin: namque aliis aliud retro quoque taetrius esset
en: for one thing would also be more loathsome than another, in reverse,

latin: naribus auribus atque oculis orisque sapori.
en: to nostrils, ears and eyes, and to the taste of the mouth.

latin: quae quoniam non sunt, sed rebus reddita certa
en: And since these things are not so, but a fixed limit, assigned

latin: finis utrimque tenet summam, fateare necessest
en: to things, holds the sum on either side, you must admit

latin: materiem quoque finitis differe figuris.
en: that matter too differs in a finite number of shapes.

latin: denique ab ignibus ad gelidas hiemum usque pruinas
en: Finally, from fires to the freezing frosts of winters

latin: finitumst retroque pari ratione remensumst.
en: the way is bounded, and measured back again in equal measure.

latin: omnis enim calor ac frigus mediique tepores
en: For all heat and cold and the middle warmths

latin: interutrasque iacent explentes ordine summam.
en: lie between the two, filling out the sum in order.

latin: ergo finita distant ratione creata,
en: Therefore created things differ within a finite range,

latin: ancipiti quoniam mucroni utrimque notantur,
en: since at both ends they are marked by a two-edged point,

latin: hinc flammis illinc rigidis infesta pruinis.
en: beset by flames on this side and on that by stiff frosts.

latin: Quod quoniam docui, pergam conectere rem quae
en: Since I have taught this, I will go on to join to it a fact

latin: ex hoc apta fidem ducat, primordia rerum,
en: which, fitted to this, draws its credit: that the first-beginnings of things,

latin: inter se simili quae sunt perfecta figura,
en: those that are made of a shape alike among themselves,

latin: infinita cluere. etenim distantia cum sit
en: are infinite in number. For since the difference

latin: formarum finita, necesse est quae similes sint
en: of forms is finite, it must be that those that are alike

latin: esse infinitas aut summam materiai
en: are infinite, or else that the sum of matter

latin: finitam constare, id quod non esse probavi.
en: is finite, which I have proved is not so.

latin: versibus ostendam corpuscula materiai
en: I will show in verses that the little bodies of matter

latin: ex infinito summam rerum usque tenere
en: from infinity keep the sum of things going

latin: undique protelo plagarum continuato.
en: on every side, by an unbroken relay of blows.

latin: nam quod rara vides magis esse animalia quaedam
en: For as to your seeing certain animals to be rarer,

latin: fecundamque magis naturam cernis in illis,
en: and discerning in those others a nature more fruitful,

latin: at regione locoque alio terrisque remotis
en: yet in another region and place, in far-off lands,

latin: multa licet genere esse in eo numerumque repleri;
en: there may be many of that kind, and the number made up;

latin: sicut quadripedum cum primis esse videmus
en: as among four-footed beasts we see, first of all,

latin: in genere anguimanus elephantos, India quorum
en: the kind of snake-handed elephants, by whose many thousands

latin: milibus e multis vallo munitur eburno,
en: India is fortified with a rampart of ivory,

latin: ut penitus nequeat penetrari: tanta ferarum
en: so that it cannot be entered deep: so great is the multitude

latin: vis est, quarum nos perpauca exempla videmus.
en: of these beasts, of which we see very few examples.

latin: sed tamen id quoque uti concedam, quam lubet esto
en: But still, to concede this too, let there be, as you please,

latin: unica res quaedem nativo corpore sola,
en: some single thing, alone in the body it was born with,

latin: cui similis toto terrarum non sit, in orbi;
en: with nothing like it in the whole round of the lands;

latin: infinita tamen nisi erit vis materiai,
en: yet unless the store of matter is infinite,

latin: unde ea progigni possit concepta, creari
en: from which it may be conceived and brought forth, it could not

latin: non poterit neque, quod super est, procrescere alique.
en: be created, nor, for the rest, grow up and be nourished.

latin: quippe etenim sumant alii finita per omne
en: For indeed, let others assume that a finite number

latin: corpora iactari unius genitalia rei,
en: of generative bodies of one thing are tossed through the whole:

latin: unde ubi qua vi et quo pacto congressa coibunt
en: from where, where, by what force, in what way will they meet and join

latin: materiae tanto in pelago turbaque aliena?
en: in so great a sea of matter, in so alien a throng?

latin: non, ut opinor, habent rationem conciliandi:
en: They have no means, I think, of making a union;

latin: sed quasi naufragiis magnis multisque coortis
en: but as, when great and many shipwrecks have arisen,

latin: disiactare solet magnum mare transtra cavernas
en: the great sea is used to toss about thwarts, hulls,

latin: antemnas prorem malos tonsasque natantis,
en: yards, prows, masts and swimming oars,

latin: per terrarum omnis oras fluitantia aplustra
en: so that along all the lands' shores the floating stern-ornaments

latin: ut videantur et indicium mortalibus edant,
en: are seen, and give mortals a warning

latin: infidi maris insidias virisque dolumque
en: to shun the snares of the faithless sea, its strength and guile,

latin: ut vitare velint, neve ullo tempore credant,
en: and never at any time to trust it,

latin: subdola cum ridet placidi pellacia ponti,
en: when the sly enticement of the calm sea laughs,

latin: sic tibi si finita semel primordia quaedam
en: so, if once you establish certain first-beginnings as finite,

latin: constitues, aevom debebunt sparsa per omnem
en: they will have to be scattered through all time

latin: disiectare aestus diversi materiai,
en: and tossed apart by the conflicting tides of matter,

latin: numquam in concilium ut possint compulsa coire
en: so that they can never be driven together into union,

latin: nec remorari in concilio nec crescere adaucta;
en: nor linger in union, nor grow by increase;

latin: quorum utrumque palam fieri manifesta docet res,
en: and that both of these happen, the plain fact openly shows,

latin: et res progigni et genitas procrescere posse.
en: that things are brought forth and, once born, can grow.

latin: esse igitur genere in quovis primordia rerum
en: Therefore in any kind you please the first-beginnings of things

latin: infinita palam est, unde omnia suppeditantur.
en: are infinite, that is plain, from which all things are furnished.

latin: Nec superare queunt motus itaque exitiales
en: And so neither can the motions of destruction prevail

latin: perpetuo neque in aeternum sepelire salutem,
en: forever, nor bury safety for eternity,

latin: nec porro rerum genitales auctificique
en: nor again can the motions that beget and increase things

latin: motus perpetuo possunt servare creata.
en: keep forever what they have created.

latin: sic aequo geritur certamine principiorum
en: So in an equal struggle of the beginnings is waged

latin: ex infinito contractum tempore bellum.
en: a war entered on from infinite time.

latin: nunc hic nunc illic superant vitalia rerum
en: Now here, now there the life-giving powers of things conquer

latin: et superantur item. miscetur funere vagor,
en: and are conquered in turn. With the funeral is mixed the wail

latin: quem pueri tollunt visentis luminis oras;
en: that infants raise as they look on the shores of light;

latin: nec nox ulla diem neque noctem aurora secutast,
en: and no night has followed day, no dawn the night,

latin: quae non audierit mixtos vagitibus aegris
en: that has not heard, mixed with the sick wailing of infants,

latin: ploratus, mortis comites et funeris atri.
en: the lamentations that attend on death and the black funeral.

latin: Illud in his obsignatum quoque rebus habere
en: This too it is fitting, in these matters, to keep sealed up

latin: convenit et memori mandatum mente tenere,
en: and to hold, entrusted to a mind that remembers:

latin: nil esse, in promptu quorum natura videtur,
en: that there is nothing whose nature is seen plainly before us

latin: quod genere ex uno consistat principiorum,
en: that consists of one kind of beginnings alone,

latin: nec quicquam quod non permixto semine constet.
en: nothing that is not made of mingled seed.

latin: et quod cumque magis vis multas possidet in se
en: And whatever possesses more forces in itself

latin: atque potestates, ita plurima principiorum
en: and more powers, the more it shows that it holds the most kinds

latin: in sese genera ac varias docet esse figuras.
en: of beginnings in itself, and the most varied shapes.

latin: Principio tellus habet in se corpora prima,
en: First of all, the earth holds in itself first bodies

latin: unde mare inmensum volventes frigora fontes
en: from which springs, rolling out their coolness, constantly renew

latin: adsidue renovent, habet ignes unde oriantur;
en: the immeasurable sea; it holds those from which fires rise;

latin: nam multis succensa locis ardent sola terrae,
en: for in many places the ground of the earth is kindled and burns,

latin: ex imis vero furit ignibus impetus Aetnae.
en: and from its depths the onrush of Etna rages with fire.

latin: tum porro nitidas fruges arbustaque laeta
en: Then further, shining crops and glad orchards

latin: gentibus humanis habet unde extollere possit,
en: it has the means to raise up for the races of men,

latin: unde etiam fluvios frondes et pabula laeta
en: and the means to offer rivers, leaves, and glad pastures

latin: montivago generi possit praebere ferarum.
en: to the mountain-roaming race of wild beasts.

latin: quare magna deum mater materque ferarum
en: Therefore the great mother of the gods, and mother of wild beasts,

latin: et nostri genetrix haec dicta est corporis una.
en: and begetter of our body, she alone has been called.

latin: Hanc veteres Graium docti cecinere poetae
en: Of her the learned poets of the Greeks of old have sung

latin: sedibus in curru biiugos agitare leones,
en: that, seated in a chariot, she drives a yoke of lions,

latin: aeris in spatio magnam pendere docentes
en: teaching by this that the great earth hangs in the space

latin: tellurem neque posse in terra sistere terram.
en: of air, and that earth cannot rest upon earth.

latin: adiunxere feras, quia quamvis effera proles
en: They yoked wild beasts to her because offspring, however wild,

latin: officiis debet molliri victa parentum.
en: must be softened, won over by the kindnesses of parents.

latin: muralique caput summum cinxere corona,
en: And they bound the top of her head with a crown of walls,

latin: eximiis munita locis quia sustinet urbes.
en: because, fortified in choice places, she bears up cities.

latin: quo nunc insigni per magnas praedita terras
en: Adorned now with this emblem, through the great lands

latin: horrifice fertur divinae matris imago.
en: the image of the divine mother is carried, inspiring dread.

latin: hanc variae gentes antiquo more sacrorum
en: Her the various peoples, by the ancient custom of their rites,

latin: Idaeam vocitant matrem Phrygiasque catervas
en: call the Idaean Mother, and give her bands of Phrygians

latin: dant comites, quia primum ex illis finibus edunt
en: as her companions, because from those regions first, they say,

latin: per terrarum orbes fruges coepisse creari.
en: crops began to be created through the circles of the earth.

latin: Gallos attribuunt, quia, numen qui violarint
en: They assign her Galli, because, of those who have outraged

latin: Matris et ingrati genitoribus inventi sint,
en: the Mother's power and been found ungrateful to their parents,

latin: significare volunt indignos esse putandos,
en: they wish to signify that they must be thought unworthy

latin: vivam progeniem qui in oras luminis edant.
en: to bring forth living offspring into the shores of light.

latin: tympana tenta tonant palmis et cymbala circum
en: Taut drums thunder under their palms, and the hollow cymbals

latin: concava, raucisonoque minantur cornua cantu,
en: all around, and horns threaten with harsh-sounding song,

latin: et Phrygio stimulat numero cava tibia mentis,
en: and the hollow pipe goads their minds with Phrygian measure,

latin: telaque praeportant, violenti signa furoris,
en: and they carry weapons before them, signs of violent frenzy,

latin: ingratos animos atque impia pectora volgi
en: so that the ungrateful minds and impious hearts of the crowd

latin: conterrere metu quae possint numine divae.
en: may be terrified with fear by the goddess's power.

latin: ergo cum primum magnas invecta per urbis
en: And so, as soon as she is carried in through great cities

latin: munificat tacita mortalis muta salute,
en: and silently enriches mortals with a wordless blessing,

latin: aere atque argento sternunt iter omne viarum
en: they strew the whole road of her way with bronze and silver,

latin: largifica stipe ditantes ninguntque rosarum
en: enriching it with bountiful alms, and snow down rose

latin: floribus umbrantes matrem comitumque catervam.
en: blossoms, shading the mother and the band of her companions.

latin: hic armata manus, Curetas nomine Grai
en: Here an armed troop, whom the Greeks speak of by the name

latin: quos memorant, Phrygias inter si forte catervas
en: of Curetes, when they happen to sport among the Phrygian bands

latin: ludunt in numerumque exultant sanguine laeti
en: and leap in measure, glad of blood,

latin: terrificas capitum quatientes numine cristas,
en: shaking the terrifying crests on their heads with their nodding,

latin: Dictaeos referunt Curetas, qui Iovis illum
en: recall the Dictaean Curetes, who are said once to have hidden

latin: vagitum in Creta quondam occultasse feruntur,
en: that famous wailing of Jupiter in Crete,

latin: cum pueri circum puerum pernice chorea
en: when, boys around the boy, in their nimble dance,

latin: armat et in numerum pernice chorea
en: armed and in measure in their nimble dance

latin: armati in numerum pulsarent aeribus aera,
en: armed, in measure, they beat bronze upon bronze,

latin: ne Saturnus eum malis mandaret adeptus
en: so that Saturn might not catch him and give him to his jaws

latin: aeternumque daret matri sub pectore volnus.
en: and deal the Mother an eternal wound beneath her breast.

latin: propterea magnam armati matrem comitantur,
en: For this reason they attend the great mother armed,

latin: aut quia significant divam praedicere ut armis
en: or else because they signify that the goddess proclaims that with arms

latin: ac virtute velint patriam defendere terram
en: and courage men should be willing to defend their native land

latin: praesidioque parent decorique parentibus esse.
en: and make ready to be a protection and an honor to their parents.

latin: quae bene et eximie quamvis disposta ferantur,
en: These things, however well and excellently they are set out,

latin: longe sunt tamen a vera ratione repulsa.
en: are nonetheless driven far from true reasoning.

latin: omnis enim per se divom natura necessest
en: For the whole nature of the gods must, of itself, by necessity

latin: inmortali aevo summa cum pace fruatur
en: enjoy immortal life in utmost peace,

latin: semota ab nostris rebus seiunctaque longe;
en: removed from our affairs and separated far away;

latin: nam privata dolore omni, privata periclis,
en: for free from every pain, free from dangers,

latin: ipsa suis pollens opibus, nihil indiga nostri,
en: strong in its own resources, needing nothing of ours,

latin: nec bene promeritis capitur neque tangitur ira.
en: it is neither won by services nor touched by anger.

latin: terra quidem vero caret omni tempore sensu,
en: The earth, indeed, is at all times without sense,

latin: et quia multarum potitur primordia rerum,
en: and because it possesses the first-beginnings of many things,

latin: multa modis multis effert in lumina solis.
en: it brings forth many in many ways into the light of the sun.

latin: hic siquis mare Neptunum Cereremque vocare
en: Here, if anyone resolves to call the sea Neptune, and to call

latin: constituet fruges et Bacchi nomine abuti
en: the crops Ceres, and would rather misuse the name of Bacchus

latin: mavolt quam laticis proprium proferre vocamen,
en: than speak the proper word for that liquor,

latin: concedamus ut hic terrarum dictitet orbem
en: let us grant that he may keep declaring the round of the earth

latin: esse deum matrem, dum vera re tamen ipse
en: to be the mother of the gods, if only in truth he himself

latin: religione animum turpi contingere parcat.
en: refrains from tainting his mind with foul religion.

latin: Saepe itaque ex uno tondentes gramina campo
en: Thus often, cropping grass from a single field,

latin: lanigerae pecudes et equorum duellica proles
en: wool-bearing flocks and the warlike offspring of horses

latin: buceriaeque greges eodem sub tegmine caeli
en: and horned herds, beneath the same covering of sky,

latin: ex unoque sitim sedantes flumine aquai
en: quenching their thirst from a single stream of water,

latin: dissimili vivont specie retinentque parentum
en: live unlike in appearance, and keep their parents'

latin: naturam et mores generatim quaeque imitantur.
en: nature, and each, kind by kind, copies their ways.

latin: tanta est in quovis genere herbae materiai
en: So great in any kind of grass is the unlike order

latin: dissimilis ratio, tanta est in flumine quoque.
en: of matter, so great in any river too.

latin: Hinc porro quamvis animantem ex omnibus unam
en: Again, any one living creature, whichever of them all,

latin: ossa cruor venae calor umor viscera nervi
en: bones, blood, veins, heat, moisture, flesh, and sinews

latin: constituunt, quae sunt porro distantia longe,
en: make up, which are again far distant from one another,

latin: dissimili perfecta figura principiorum.
en: formed of unlike shapes of beginnings.

latin: Tum porro quae cumque igni flammata cremantur.
en: Then further, all things that are set aflame by fire and burn,

latin: si nil praeterea, tamen haec in corpore tradunt,
en: if nothing else, still carry these in their body:

latin: unde ignem iacere et lumen submittere possint
en: the means by which they can throw out fire and send up light,

latin: scintillasque agere ac late differre favillam.
en: and drive off sparks and scatter ash far and wide.

latin: cetera consimili mentis ratione peragrans
en: Going through the rest by a like reasoning of mind,

latin: invenies igitur multarum semina rerum
en: you will therefore find that they hide the seeds of many things

latin: corpore celare et varias cohibere figuras.
en: in their body, and contain varied shapes.

latin: Denique multa vides, quibus et color et sapor una
en: Finally, you see many things in which color and taste together

latin: reddita sunt cum odore in primis pleraque poma.
en: are given along with smell; first of all, most fruits.

latin: haec igitur variis debent constare figuris;
en: These, therefore, must consist of varied shapes;

latin: nidor enim penetrat qua fucus non it in artus,
en: for smell gets into our limbs where color does not go,

latin: fucus item sorsum, sorsum sapor insinuatur
en: color, likewise, apart, and taste apart, works its way

latin: sensibus; ut noscas primis differre figuris.
en: into our senses; so you may know they differ in their first shapes.

latin: dissimiles igitur formae glomeramen in unum
en: Therefore unlike forms come together into one mass,

latin: conveniunt et res permixto semine constant.
en: and things are made up out of mingled seed.

latin: Quin etiam passim nostris in versibus ipsis
en: Indeed, everywhere in these very verses of ours

latin: multa elementa vides multis communia verbis,
en: you see many elements common to many words,

latin: cum tamen inter se versus ac verba necesse est
en: though you must still admit that verses and words

latin: confiteare alia ex aliis constare elementis;
en: are made, one and another, from different elements;

latin: non quo multa parum communis littera currat
en: not because few letters run in common among them,

latin: aut nulla inter se duo sint ex omnibus isdem,
en: or no two are made out of letters entirely the same,

latin: sed quia non volgo paria omnibus omnia constant.
en: but because, as a rule, not all are alike to all.

latin: sic aliis in rebus item communia multa
en: So likewise in other things, since many are common

latin: multarum rerum cum sint, primordia rerum
en: to many things, the first-beginnings of things

latin: dissimili tamen inter se consistere summa
en: can nonetheless make up, among themselves, unlike wholes;

latin: possunt; ut merito ex aliis constare feratur
en: so that it may rightly be said that the human race

latin: humanum genus et fruges arbustaque laeta.
en: and crops and glad orchards are made of different things.

latin: Nec tamen omnimodis conecti posse putandum est
en: Yet we must not think that all things can be joined

latin: omnia; nam volgo fieri portenta videres,
en: in every way; for you would see monsters everywhere come to be,

latin: semiferas hominum species existere et altos
en: forms half beast, half man spring up, and tall

latin: inter dum ramos egigni corpore vivo
en: branches at times put forth from a living body,

latin: multaque conecti terrestria membra marinis,
en: and many limbs of land creatures joined to those of the sea,

latin: tum flammam taetro spirantis ore Chimaeras
en: and then Chimaeras, breathing flame from their foul mouths,

latin: pascere naturam per terras omniparentis.
en: and nature feeding them across the all-mothering lands.

latin: quorum nil fieri manifestum est, omnia quando
en: It is plain that none of this happens, since all things

latin: seminibus certis certa genetrice creata
en: created from fixed seeds and by a fixed mother,

latin: conservare genus crescentia posse videmus.
en: can, we see, preserve their kind as they grow.

latin: scilicet id certa fieri ratione necessust.
en: Clearly this must come about by a fixed principle.

latin: nam sua cuique cibis ex omnibus intus in artus
en: For to each, out of all its foods, its own bodies pass

latin: corpora discedunt conexaque convenientis
en: within, into the limbs, and, once joined, produce

latin: efficiunt motus; at contra aliena videmus
en: the fitting motions; but against this we see nature

latin: reicere in terras naturam, multaque caecis
en: cast out onto the earth what is alien, and many things, in unseen

latin: corporibus fugiunt e corpore percita plagis,
en: bodies, flee out of the body, driven by blows,

latin: quae neque conecti quoquam potuere neque intus
en: which could neither be joined anywhere nor, within,

latin: vitalis motus consentire atque imitari.
en: feel with the vital motions and imitate them.

latin: sed ne forte putes animalia sola teneri
en: But lest you think that only living things are held

latin: legibus his, quaedam ratio res terminat omnis
en: by these laws, a certain principle bounds all things.

latin: nam vel uti tota natura dissimiles sunt
en: For just as things begotten are unlike one another

latin: inter se genitae res quaeque, ita quamque necessest
en: in their whole nature, each of them, so each must

latin: dissimili constare figura principiorum;
en: be made of unlike shapes of beginnings;

latin: non quo multa parum simili sint praedita forma,
en: not that few are endowed with a like form,

latin: sed quia non volgo paria omnibus omnia constant.
en: but because, as a rule, not all are alike to all.

latin: semina cum porro distent, differre necessust
en: Further, since the seeds differ, there must be differences in

latin: intervalla vias conexus pondera plagas
en: intervals, paths, connections, weights, blows,

latin: concursus motus; quae non animalia solum
en: collisions, motions; which not only divide living bodies

latin: corpora seiungunt, sed terras ac mare totum
en: from one another, but keep the lands and the whole sea

latin: secernunt caelumque a terris omne retentant.
en: apart, and hold back the whole heaven from the lands.

latin: Nunc age dicta meo dulci quaesita labore
en: Come now, take in these words, sought out by my sweet labor,

latin: percipe, ne forte haec albis ex alba rearis
en: so that you do not by chance suppose the white things are from white

latin: principiis esse, ante oculos quae candida cernis,
en: beginnings, the things you see shining before your eyes,

latin: aut ea quae nigrant nigro de semine nata;
en: or that the things that are black are born of black seed;

latin: nive alium quemvis quae sunt inbuta colorem,
en: or that whatever is steeped in any other color

latin: propterea gerere hunc credas, quod materiai
en: bears it because the bodies of matter

latin: corpora consimili sint eius tincta colore;
en: are dyed with a color just like its own;

latin: nullus enim color est omnino materiai
en: for the bodies of matter have no color

latin: corporibus, neque par rebus neque denique dispar.
en: at all, neither like things nor, finally, unlike them.

latin: in quae corpora si nullus tibi forte videtur
en: And if it seems to you perhaps that upon these bodies no casting

latin: posse animi iniectus fieri, procul avius erras.
en: of the mind can be made, you wander far out of the way.

latin: nam cum caecigeni, solis qui lumina numquam
en: For since the blind from birth, who have never looked upon

latin: dispexere, tamen cognoscant corpora tactu
en: the light of the sun, still come to know bodies by touch

latin: ex ineunte aevo nullo coniuncta colore,
en: that from the beginning of life were joined with no color,

latin: scire licet nostrae quoque menti corpora posse
en: you may know that bodies can also come into the notice

latin: vorti in notitiam nullo circum lita fuco.
en: of our mind, though smeared about with no dye.

latin: denique nos ipsi caecis quaecumque tenebris
en: Finally, whatever we ourselves touch in blind darkness

latin: tangimus, haud ullo sentimus tincta colore.
en: we do not perceive as dyed with any color.

latin: Quod quoniam vinco fieri, nunc esse docebo.
en: Since I prove that this can be, I shall now show that it is so.

latin: omnis enim color omnino mutatur in omnis;
en: For every color changes, all of it, into every other;

latin: quod facere haud ullo debent primordia pacto;
en: this the first-beginnings must by no means do;

latin: immutabile enim quiddam superare necessest,
en: for something unchangeable must survive,

latin: ne res ad nihilum redigantur funditus omnes;
en: so that things are not all brought back utterly to nothing;

latin: nam quod cumque suis mutatum finibus exit,
en: for whatever is changed and passes out of its own bounds,

latin: continuo hoc mors est illius quod fuit ante.
en: this at once is the death of what it was before.

latin: proinde colore cave contingas semina rerum,
en: Therefore take care not to touch the seeds of things with color,

latin: ne tibi res redeant ad nihilum funditus omnes.
en: so that all things do not return utterly to nothing for you.

latin: Praeterea si nulla coloris principiis est
en: Further, if no nature of color has been given

latin: reddita natura et variis sunt praedita formis,
en: to the beginnings, and they are endowed with various forms,

latin: e quibus omnigenus gignunt variantque colores,
en: from which they beget colors of every kind and vary them,

latin: propterea magni quod refert, semina quaeque
en: therefore, since it matters greatly for each of the seeds

latin: cum quibus et quali positura contineantur
en: with what and in what position they are held together,

latin: et quos inter se dent motus accipiantque,
en: and what motions they give and receive among themselves,

latin: perfacile extemplo rationem reddere possis,
en: at once you could most easily give the reason

latin: cur ea quae nigro fuerint paulo ante colore,
en: why things that were of a black color a little before

latin: marmoreo fieri possint candore repente,
en: can suddenly become of a marble whiteness,

latin: ut mare, cum magni commorunt aequora venti,
en: as the sea, when great winds have stirred its levels,

latin: vertitur in canos candenti marmore fluctus;
en: is turned into white waves of shining marble;

latin: dicere enim possis, nigrum quod saepe videmus,
en: for you could say that what we often see as black,

latin: materies ubi permixta est illius et ordo
en: when its matter has been mixed through, and the order

latin: principiis mutatus et addita demptaque quaedam,
en: of the beginnings changed, and certain things added and taken away,

latin: continuo id fieri ut candens videatur et album.
en: at once comes to be seen as shining and white.

latin: quod si caeruleis constarent aequora ponti
en: But if the levels of the sea consisted of blue

latin: seminibus, nullo possent albescere pacto;
en: seeds, they could in no way grow white;

latin: nam quo cumque modo perturbes caerula quae sint,
en: for however you stir up things that are blue,

latin: numquam in marmoreum possunt migrare colorem.
en: they can never pass over into the color of marble.

latin: sin alio atque alio sunt semina tincta colore,
en: But if the seeds are dyed with one color and another

latin: quae maris efficiunt unum purumque nitorem,
en: that make the sea's one pure brightness,

latin: ut saepe ex aliis formis variisque figuris
en: as often from other forms and various shapes

latin: efficitur quiddam quadratum unaque figura,
en: something square and of a single shape is made,

latin: conveniebat, ut in quadrato cernimus esse
en: it would be fitting that, as we see in the square

latin: dissimiles formas, ita cernere in aequore ponti
en: unlike forms, so we should see in the level of the sea,

latin: aut alio in quovis uno puroque nitore
en: or in any other single and pure brightness,

latin: dissimiles longe inter se variosque colores.
en: colors widely unlike one another and various.

latin: praeterea nihil officiunt obstantque figurae
en: Further, unlike shapes do not hinder or stand in the way

latin: dissimiles, quo quadratum minus omne sit extra;
en: of the whole being square on the outside;

latin: at varii rerum inpediunt prohibentque colores,
en: but the various colors of things hinder and prevent

latin: quo minus esse uno possit res tota nitore.
en: the whole thing from being of a single brightness.

latin: Tum porro quae ducit et inlicit ut tribuamus
en: Then again the cause that leads and lures us to assign

latin: principiis rerum non numquam causa colores,
en: colors at times to the beginnings of things

latin: occidit, ex albis quoniam non alba creantur,
en: falls dead, since white things are not created from white,

latin: nec quae nigra cluent de nigris, sed variis ex.
en: nor things called black from black, but from various.

latin: quippe etenim multo proclivius exorientur
en: For indeed white things will arise much more readily

latin: candida de nullo quam nigro nata colore
en: born of no color than of black

latin: aut alio quovis, qui contra pugnet et obstet.
en: or of any other that fights against them and stands in the way.

latin: Praeterea quoniam nequeunt sine luce colores
en: Further, since colors cannot be without light,

latin: esse neque in lucem existunt primordia rerum,
en: and the first-beginnings of things do not come out into the light,

latin: scire licet quam sint nullo velata colore;
en: you may know that they are veiled with no color;

latin: qualis enim caecis poterit color esse tenebris?
en: for what color can there be in blind darkness?

latin: lumine quin ipso mutatur propterea quod
en: Indeed, color is changed by the light itself, according as

latin: recta aut obliqua percussus luce refulget;
en: it shines back, struck by a straight or a slanting light;

latin: pluma columbarum quo pacto in sole videtur,
en: as the plumage of doves is seen in the sun,

latin: quae sita cervices circum collumque coronat;
en: the plumage that, set about the nape, crowns the neck;

latin: namque alias fit uti claro sit rubra pyropo,
en: for at times it comes to be red with bright fire-bronze,

latin: inter dum quodam sensu fit uti videatur
en: at times, to a certain way of seeing, it comes to seem

latin: inter caeruleum viridis miscere zmaragdos.
en: to mingle green emeralds with the blue.

latin: caudaque pavonis, larga cum luce repleta est,
en: And the peacock's tail, when it is filled with plentiful light,

latin: consimili mutat ratione obversa colores;
en: changes its colors by a like principle as it turns;

latin: qui quoniam quodam gignuntur luminis ictu,
en: and since these colors are begotten by a certain stroke of light,

latin: scire licet, sine eo fieri non posse putandum est.
en: you may know it must be thought they cannot come to be without it.

latin: Et quoniam plagae quoddam genus excipit in se
en: And since the pupil receives into itself a certain kind of blow

latin: pupula, cum sentire colorem dicitur album,
en: when it is said to perceive the color white,

latin: atque aliud porro, nigrum cum et cetera sentit,
en: and again another when it perceives black and the rest,

latin: nec refert ea quae tangas quo forte colore
en: and it does not matter with what color the things you touch

latin: praedita sint, verum quali magis apta figura,
en: may chance to be endowed, but rather with what shape they are fitted,

latin: scire licet nihil principiis opus esse colore,
en: you may know that the beginnings have no need of color,

latin: sed variis formis variantes edere tactus.
en: but give out various touches by their various forms.

latin: Praeterea quoniam non certis certa figuris
en: Further, since no fixed nature of color belongs to fixed

latin: est natura coloris et omnia principiorum
en: shapes, and all the formings of the beginnings

latin: formamenta queunt in quovis esse nitore,
en: can be in any brightness whatever,

latin: cur ea quae constant ex illis non pariter sunt
en: why are the things composed of them not likewise

latin: omnigenus perfusa coloribus in genere omni?
en: steeped in colors of every sort, in every kind of thing?

latin: conveniebat enim corvos quoque saepe volantis
en: For it would be fitting that ravens too, as they fly, should often

latin: ex albis album pinnis iactare colorem
en: throw off a white color from white feathers,

latin: et nigros fieri nigro de semine cycnos
en: and that swans should become black from black seed,

latin: aut alio quovis uno varioque colore.
en: or of any other color, single or varied.

latin: Quin etiam quanto in partes res quaeque minutas
en: Moreover, the more each thing is pulled apart into tiny parts,

latin: distrahitur magis, hoc magis est ut cernere possis
en: the more it is that you can see

latin: evanescere paulatim stinguique colorem;
en: the color fade little by little and be quenched;

latin: ut fit ubi in parvas partis discerpitur austrum:
en: as happens when purple cloth is torn into small parts:

latin: purpura poeniceusque color clarissimus multo,
en: the purple, and the scarlet, much the brightest of colors,

latin: filatim cum distractum est, disperditur omnis;
en: when pulled apart thread by thread, is wholly lost;

latin: noscere ut hinc possis prius omnem efflare colorem
en: so that from this you may learn that all their color is breathed out

latin: particulas, quam discedant ad semina rerum.
en: by the small pieces before they part into the seeds of things.

latin: Postremo quoniam non omnia corpora vocem
en: Lastly, since you grant that not all bodies send out

latin: mittere concedis neque odorem, propterea fit
en: a voice, nor a smell, it comes about, therefore,

latin: ut non omnibus adtribuas sonitus et odores:
en: that you do not assign sounds and smells to all:

latin: sic oculis quoniam non omnia cernere quimus,
en: so, since we cannot perceive all things with our eyes,

latin: scire licet quaedam tam constare orba colore
en: you may know that some things are as bereft of color

latin: quam sine odore ullo quaedam sonituque remota,
en: as some are without any smell and removed from sound,

latin: nec minus haec animum cognoscere posse sagacem
en: and that the keen mind can come to know these no less

latin: quam quae sunt aliis rebus privata notare.
en: than it can mark the things deprived of other qualities.

latin: Sed ne forte putes solo spoliata colore
en: But in case you should think that, stripped of color alone,

latin: corpora prima manere, etiam secreta teporis
en: the first bodies remain so, they are also set apart from warmth

latin: sunt ac frigoris omnino calidique vaporis,
en: and from cold entirely, and from burning heat;

latin: et sonitu sterila et suco ieiuna feruntur,
en: they go barren of sound and starved of flavor,

latin: nec iaciunt ullum proprium de corpore odorem.
en: and give off from their body no odor of their own.

latin: sicut amaracini blandum stactaeque liquorem
en: Just as, for the soothing liquor of marjoram and of myrrh

latin: et nardi florem, nectar qui naribus halat,
en: and the flower of nard, which breathes nectar to the nostrils,

latin: cum facere instituas, cum primis quaerere par est,
en: when you set about making them, it is right first to seek,

latin: quod licet ac possis reperire, inolentis olivi
en: as far as you may and can find it, an odorless olive oil,

latin: naturam, nullam quae mittat naribus auram,
en: whose nature sends out no breath at all to the nostrils,

latin: quam minime ut possit mixtos in corpore odores
en: so that it may least of all spoil the odors mixed in its body

latin: concoctosque suo contractans perdere viro,
en: and blended there, by touching them with its own rankness,

latin: propter eandem rem debent primordia rerum
en: for the same reason the first-beginnings of things must

latin: non adhibere suum gignundis rebus odorem
en: not lend their own odor to the things they beget,

latin: nec sonitum, quoniam nihil ab se mittere possunt,
en: nor sound, since they can send out nothing from themselves,

latin: nec simili ratione saporem denique quemquam
en: nor, on a like principle, finally, any flavor at all,

latin: nec frigus neque item calidum tepidumque vaporem,
en: nor cold, nor likewise hot and tepid heat,

latin: cetera, quae cum ita sunt tamen ut mortalia constent,
en: and all the rest: things which are still such as to be mortal,

latin: molli lenta, fragosa putri, cava corpore raro,
en: pliant with soft, brittle with crumbling, hollow with porous body,

latin: omnia sint a principiis seiuncta necessest,
en: all these must be kept apart from the beginnings,

latin: inmortalia si volumus subiungere rebus
en: if we wish to set beneath things foundations immortal,

latin: fundamenta, quibus nitatur summa salutis;
en: on which the whole of their safety may rest;

latin: ne tibi res redeant ad nihilum funditus omnes.
en: so that all things do not return utterly to nothing for you.

latin: Nunc ea quae sentire videmus cumque necessest
en: Now all the things we see to have sense, whatever they are,

latin: ex insensilibus tamen omnia confiteare
en: you must confess are, for all that, made up of senseless

latin: principiis constare. neque id manufesta refutant
en: beginnings. Nor do plain facts refute this

latin: nec contra pugnant, in promptu cognita quae sunt,
en: or fight against it, the things known and ready to hand;

latin: sed magis ipsa manu ducunt et credere cogunt
en: rather they themselves lead us by the hand and compel belief

latin: ex insensilibus, quod dico, animalia gigni.
en: that, as I say, living creatures are born from senseless things.

latin: quippe videre licet vivos existere vermes
en: Indeed, you can see living worms come forth

latin: stercore de taetro, putorem cum sibi nacta est
en: out of foul dung, when a rottenness has come over

latin: intempestivis ex imbribus umida tellus.
en: the sodden earth from untimely rains.

latin: Praeterea cunctas itidem res vertere sese.
en: Further, all things in like manner turn themselves into others.

latin: vertunt se fluvii in frondes et pabula laeta
en: Rivers turn themselves into leaves, and glad pastures

latin: in pecudes, vertunt pecudes in corpora nostra
en: into cattle; cattle turn into our bodies

latin: naturam, et nostro de corpore saepe ferarum
en: their nature, and from our body often the strength of wild beasts

latin: augescunt vires et corpora pennipotentum.
en: grows, and the bodies of the strong-winged birds.

latin: ergo omnes natura cibos in corpora viva
en: Therefore nature turns all foods into living bodies

latin: vertit et hinc sensus animantum procreat omnes,
en: and from them brings forth all the senses of living things,

latin: non alia longe ratione atque arida ligna
en: on a principle not far other than that by which

latin: explicat in flammas et in ignis omnia versat.
en: it unfolds dry logs into flames and turns them all to fire.

latin: iamne vides igitur magni primordia rerum
en: Do you see now, therefore, that for the first-beginnings of things

latin: referre in quali sint ordine quaeque locata
en: it matters greatly in what order each is set

latin: et commixta quibus dent motus accipiantque?
en: and mixed with what, and what motions they give and take?

latin: Tum porro, quid id est, animum quod percutit, ipsum,
en: Then further, what is it that strikes the mind itself,

latin: quod movet et varios sensus expromere cogit,
en: that moves it and compels it to give out various senses,

latin: ex insensilibus ne credas sensile gigni?
en: so that you do not believe the sentient is born from the senseless?

latin: ni mirum lapides et ligna et terra quod una
en: Surely it is that stones and wood and earth, mixed

latin: mixta tamen nequeunt vitalem reddere sensum.
en: together, still cannot give back the sense of life.

latin: illud in his igitur rebus meminisse decebit,
en: In these matters, then, it will be fitting to remember this:

latin: non ex omnibus omnino, quaecumque creant res
en: not from any and all things whatever that create

latin: sensilia, extemplo me gigni dicere sensus,
en: sentient things do I say that senses are at once begotten,

latin: sed magni referre ea primum quantula constent,
en: but that it matters greatly, first, how small are the things

latin: sensile quae faciunt, et qua sint praedita forma,
en: that make the sentient, and with what shape they are endowed,

latin: motibus ordinibus posituris denique quae sint.
en: and finally what they are in motions, orders, positions.

latin: quarum nil rerum in lignis glaebisque videmus;
en: Of these things we see none in logs and clods;

latin: et tamen haec, cum sunt quasi putrefacta per imbres,
en: and yet these, when they are as it were rotted by the rains,

latin: vermiculos pariunt, quia corpora materiai
en: give birth to little worms, because the bodies of matter,

latin: antiquis ex ordinibus permota nova re
en: stirred from their old orders by a new event,

latin: conciliantur ita ut debent animalia gigni.
en: are united as they must be for living things to be born.

latin: Deinde ex sensilibus qui sensile posse creari
en: Next, those who would have it that from sentient things the sentient

latin: constituunt, porro ex aliis sentire sueti
en: can be created, and these in turn from others used to sensing,

latin: mollia cum faciunt; nam sensus iungitur omnis
en: when they make them soft; for all sense is bound up

latin: visceribus nervis venis, quae cumque videmus
en: with flesh, sinews, veins, all of which we see

latin: mollia mortali consistere corpore creta.
en: are soft, fashioned of mortal body.

latin: sed tamen esto iam posse haec aeterna manere;
en: But still, grant now that these can remain eternal:

latin: nempe tamen debent aut sensum partis habere
en: surely, even so, they must either have the sense of a part

latin: aut similis totis animalibus esse putari.
en: or be thought to be like whole living creatures.

latin: at nequeant per se partes sentire necesse est:
en: But it must be that parts cannot have sense by themselves;

latin: namque animus sensus membrorum respuit omnis,
en: for the mind rejects all the senses of the limbs,

latin: nec manus a nobis potis est secreta neque ulla
en: nor can a hand cut off from us, nor any

latin: corporis omnino sensum pars sola tenere.
en: part of the body at all, hold sense alone.

latin: linquitur ut totis animantibus adsimulentur,
en: It remains that they be likened to whole living creatures,

latin: vitali ut possint consentire undique sensu.
en: so that they can feel in concert, everywhere, with the sense of life.

latin: qui poterunt igitur rerum primordia dici
en: How then can they be called first-beginnings of things

latin: et leti vitare vias, animalia cum sint,
en: and shun the roads of death, since they are living creatures,

latin: atque animalia sint mortalibus una eademque?
en: and living creatures are one and the same as mortal beings?

latin: quod tamen ut possint, at coetu concilioque
en: Yet even granting that they could, still by their meeting and union

latin: nil facient praeter volgum turbamque animantum,
en: they will make nothing but a crowd and throng of living things,

latin: scilicet ut nequeant homines armenta feraeque
en: just as, surely, men, herds, and wild beasts cannot

latin: inter sese ullam rem gignere conveniundo.
en: beget any other thing among themselves by coming together.

latin: sic itidem quae sentimus sentire necessest.
en: In the same way, what we sense must itself sense.

latin: quod si forte suum dimittunt corpore sensum
en: But if perhaps they put off their own sense from their body

latin: atque alium capiunt, quid opus fuit adtribui id quod
en: and take on another, what need was there to grant what

latin: detrahitur? tum praeterea, quod fudimus ante,
en: is taken away? Then further, as we set out before,
