en: inasmuch as into living chicks the eggs

latin: cernimus alituum vermisque effervere terra,
en: of birds, we see, are turned, and worms swarm out of the earth

latin: intempestivos quam putor cepit ob imbris,
en: when rottenness has seized it after untimely rains,

latin: scire licet gigni posse ex non sensibus sensus.
en: we may know that senses can be born from what is not sense.

latin: Quod si forte aliquis dicet, dum taxat oriri
en: But if perhaps someone says that sense can only arise

latin: posse ex non sensu sensus mutabilitate,
en: from what is not sense by a process of change,

latin: aut aliquo tamquam partu quod proditur extra,
en: or by a kind of birth, by which it is brought forth outward,

latin: huic satis illud erit planum facere atque probare,
en: for him it will be enough to make clear and prove this:

latin: non fieri partum nisi concilio ante coacto,
en: that no birth happens unless a union has first been formed,

latin: nec quicquam commutari sine conciliatu.
en: nor does anything change without a uniting.

latin: Principio nequeunt ullius corporis esse
en: To begin with, there can be no senses of any body

latin: sensus ante ipsam genitam naturam animantis,
en: before the nature of the living creature itself is born,

latin: ni mirum quia materies disiecta tenetur
en: surely because the matter is held scattered

latin: aere fluminibus terris terraque creatis,
en: in air, rivers, earth, and the things born of earth,

latin: nec congressa modo vitalis convenientes
en: and has not, meeting, brought together in fitting manner

latin: contulit inter se motus, quibus omnituentes
en: the vital motions among themselves, by which the all-watching

latin: accensi sensus animantem quamque tuentur.
en: senses, kindled, watch over each living creature.

latin: Praeterea quamvis animantem grandior ictus,
en: Further, any living creature a blow too great

latin: quam patitur natura, repente adfligit et omnis
en: for its nature to bear strikes down suddenly, and goes on

latin: corporis atque animi pergit confundere sensus.
en: to throw into confusion all the senses of body and mind.

latin: dissoluuntur enim positurae principiorum
en: For the positions of the beginnings are dissolved,

latin: et penitus motus vitales inpediuntur,
en: and the vital motions are hindered deep within,

latin: donec materies omnis concussa per artus
en: until all the matter, shaken through the limbs,

latin: vitalis animae nodos a corpore solvit
en: loosens the knots of the vital spirit from the body

latin: dispersamque foras per caulas eiecit omnis;
en: and casts it out, scattered abroad, through all the passages;

latin: nam quid praeterea facere ictum posse reamur
en: for what else should we think a blow can do,

latin: oblatum, nisi discutere ac dissolvere quaeque?
en: when it is dealt, but shatter and dissolve each thing?

latin: fit quoque uti soleant minus oblato acriter ictu
en: It happens too that, when a blow is dealt less sharply,

latin: reliqui motus vitalis vincere saepe,
en: the vital motions that remain will often win,

latin: vincere et ingentis plagae sedare tumultus
en: win and calm the vast tumults of the stroke,

latin: inque suos quicquid rursus revocare meatus
en: and call each part back again into its own paths,

latin: et quasi iam leti dominantem in corpore motum
en: and the motion of death, already, as it were, master in the body,

latin: discutere ac paene amissos accendere sensus;
en: shake apart, and kindle the senses almost lost;

latin: nam qua re potius leti iam limine ab ipso
en: for by what means could they rather, from death's very threshold,

latin: ad vitam possint conlecta mente reverti,
en: gather their mind and come back to life

latin: quam quo decursum prope iam siet ire et abire?
en: than go on and depart where their course is almost run?

latin: Praeterea, quoniam dolor est, ubi materiai
en: Further, since pain exists when bodies of matter,

latin: corpora vi quadam per viscera viva per artus
en: by some force, through the living flesh, through the limbs,

latin: sollicitata suis trepidant in sedibus intus,
en: are troubled and tremble within, in their own seats,

latin: inque locum quando remigrant, fit blanda voluptas,
en: and when they move back into place a soothing pleasure comes,

latin: scire licet nullo primordia posse dolore
en: we may know that the first-beginnings can be assailed

latin: temptari nullamque voluptatem capere ex se;
en: by no pain, and take no pleasure from themselves;

latin: quandoquidem non sunt ex ullis principiorum
en: since they are not made out of any bodies of beginnings,

latin: corporibus, quorum motus novitate laborent
en: bodies, through the novelty of whose motions they might suffer

latin: aut aliquem fructum capiant dulcedinis almae.
en: or reap some fruit of nourishing sweetness.

latin: haut igitur debent esse ullo praedita sensu.
en: They ought not, therefore, to be endowed with any sense.

latin: Denique uti possint sentire animalia quaeque,
en: Finally, so that every living creature can feel,

latin: principiis si iam est sensus tribuendus eorum,
en: if sense must now be granted to their beginnings,

latin: quid, genus humanum propritim de quibus auctumst?
en: what of those that make up the human race in particular?

latin: scilicet et risu tremulo concussa cachinnant
en: No doubt they too must shake with trembling laughter and guffaw,

latin: et lacrimis spargunt rorantibus ora genasque
en: and sprinkle their faces and cheeks with dewy tears,

latin: multaque de rerum mixtura dicere callent
en: and be skilled at saying much about the mixture of things,

latin: et sibi proporro quae sint primordia quaerunt;
en: and go on to ask what their own first-beginnings are;

latin: quando quidem totis mortalibus adsimulata
en: since, made in the likeness of whole mortals,

latin: ipsa quoque ex aliis debent constare elementis,
en: they too in their turn must consist of other elements,

latin: inde alia ex aliis, nusquam consistere ut ausis;
en: and those again of others, so that you never dare to stop;

latin: quippe sequar, quod cumque loqui ridereque dices
en: for I shall press you: whatever you say can speak and laugh

latin: et sapere, ex aliis eadem haec facientibus ut sit.
en: and be wise must be made of others that do these same things.

latin: quod si delira haec furiosaque cernimus esse
en: But if we see that this is raving and madness,

latin: et ridere potest non ex ridentibus auctus,
en: and a man can laugh though not made of laughing things,

latin: et sapere et doctis rationem reddere dictis
en: and be wise and give an account in learned words

latin: non ex seminibus sapientibus atque disertis,
en: though not made of seeds that are wise and eloquent,

latin: qui minus esse queant ea quae sentire videmus
en: why should the things we see have sense be any less able

latin: seminibus permixta carentibus undique sensu?
en: to be of seeds mixed together that lack sense in every part?

latin: Denique caelesti sumus omnes semine oriundi;
en: Finally, we are all sprung from heavenly seed;

latin: omnibus ille idem pater est, unde alma liquentis
en: all have that same father, from whom the nourishing mother,

latin: umoris guttas mater cum terra recepit,
en: earth, when she has received the liquid drops of moisture,

latin: feta parit nitidas fruges arbustaque laeta
en: teems and bears the shining grain and the glad trees

latin: et genus humanum, parit omnia saecla ferarum,
en: and the human race, bears all the generations of wild beasts,

latin: pabula cum praebet, quibus omnes corpora pascunt
en: since she provides the pastures on which all feed their bodies

latin: et dulcem ducunt vitam prolemque propagant;
en: and lead a sweet life and propagate their offspring;

latin: qua propter merito maternum nomen adepta est.
en: therefore she has rightly gained the name of mother.

latin: cedit item retro, de terra quod fuit ante,
en: Likewise what came from the earth before goes back

latin: in terras, et quod missumst ex aetheris oris,
en: into the earth, and what was sent from the shores of the ether

latin: id rursum caeli rellatum templa receptant.
en: is carried back again and received by the precincts of heaven.

latin: nec sic interemit mors res ut materiai
en: Nor does death so destroy things as to annihilate

latin: corpora conficiat, sed coetum dissupat ollis;
en: the bodies of matter, but it scatters their union;

latin: inde aliis aliud coniungit et efficit, omnis
en: then it joins one to another and brings it about that all

latin: res ut convertant formas mutentque colores
en: things change their shapes and alter their colors

latin: et capiant sensus et puncto tempore reddant;
en: and take on sense and in an instant give it up;

latin: ut noscas referre earum primordia rerum
en: so that you may know it matters, for the first-beginnings of things,

latin: cum quibus et quali positura contineantur
en: with what and in what position they are held together,

latin: et quos inter se dent motus accipiantque,
en: and what motions they give and receive among themselves,

latin: neve putes aeterna penes residere potesse
en: and may not think that there can reside in eternal

latin: corpora prima quod in summis fluitare videmus
en: first bodies what we see floating on the surfaces

latin: rebus et interdum nasci subitoque perire.
en: of things, and at times being born and suddenly perishing.

latin: quin etiam refert nostris in versibus ipsis
en: Indeed, even in my verses themselves it matters

latin: cum quibus et quali sint ordine quaeque locata;
en: with what and in what order each is placed;

latin: namque eadem caelum mare terras flumina solem
en: for the same ones signify heaven, sea, lands, rivers, sun,

latin: significant, eadem fruges arbusta animantis;
en: the same signify grain, trees, living creatures;

latin: si non omnia sunt, at multo maxima pars est
en: if not all, yet by far the greatest part

latin: consimilis; verum positura discrepitant res.
en: are alike; but by their position the things differ.

latin: sic ipsis in rebus item iam materiai
en: So too in things themselves, when of matter

latin: intervalla vias conexus pondera plagas
en: the intervals, paths, connections, weights, blows,

latin: concursus motus ordo positura figurae
en: collisions, motions, order, position, shapes

latin: cum permutantur, mutari res quoque debent.
en: are changed, the things too must be changed.

latin: Nunc animum nobis adhibe veram ad rationem.
en: Now apply your mind, for me, to true reasoning.

latin: nam tibi vehementer nova res molitur ad auris
en: For a thing strikingly new is struggling to reach

latin: accedere et nova se species ostendere rerum.
en: your ears, and a new face of things to show itself.

latin: sed neque tam facilis res ulla est, quin ea primum
en: But there is no thing so easy that it does not at first

latin: difficilis magis ad credendum constet, itemque
en: prove harder to believe, and likewise

latin: nil adeo magnum neque tam mirabile quicquam,
en: nothing so great, nothing so wonderful,

latin: quod non paulatim minuant mirarier omnes,
en: that all do not little by little lessen their wonder at it.

latin: principio caeli clarum purumque colorem
en: Consider first the clear and pure color of the sky,

latin: quaeque in se cohibet, palantia sidera passim,
en: and all it holds within it, the stars wandering everywhere,

latin: lunamque et solis praeclara luce nitorem;
en: and the moon, and the sun's brightness with its glorious light;

latin: omnia quae nunc si primum mortalibus essent
en: all of which, if now for the first time to mortals,

latin: ex improviso si sint obiecta repente,
en: if they were suddenly thrown before them unforeseen,

latin: quid magis his rebus poterat mirabile dici,
en: what could be called more wonderful than these things,

latin: aut minus ante quod auderent fore credere gentes?
en: or what would the nations less have dared beforehand to believe could be?

latin: nil, ut opinor; ita haec species miranda fuisset.
en: Nothing, I think: so wondrous would this appearance have been.

latin: quam tibi iam nemo fessus satiate videndi,
en: Yet now, wearied with the surfeit of seeing, no one

latin: suspicere in caeli dignatur lucida templa.
en: deigns to look up at the shining precincts of heaven.

latin: desine qua propter novitate exterritus ipsa
en: Cease, therefore, frightened by mere newness,

latin: expuere ex animo rationem, sed magis acri
en: to spit reasoning out of your mind, but rather with keen

latin: iudicio perpende, et si tibi vera videntur,
en: judgment weigh it, and if it seems true to you,

latin: dede manus, aut, si falsum est, accingere contra.
en: give in; or, if it is false, gird yourself against it.

latin: quaerit enim rationem animus, cum summa loci sit
en: For the mind seeks reasoning, since the sum of place

latin: infinita foris haec extra moenia mundi,
en: is infinite outside, beyond these walls of the world,

latin: quid sit ibi porro, quo prospicere usque velit mens
en: of what is there further, where thought longs to look ever onward

latin: atque animi iactus liber quo pervolet ipse.
en: and where the free cast of the mind itself flies through.

latin: Principio nobis in cunctas undique partis
en: First of all, for us in every direction all around,

latin: et latere ex utroque supra supterque per omne
en: on either side, above and below, through the whole,

latin: nulla est finis; uti docui, res ipsaque per se
en: there is no limit; as I have taught, and the thing itself

latin: vociferatur, et elucet natura profundi.
en: cries aloud, and the nature of the deep shines clear.

latin: nullo iam pacto veri simile esse putandumst,
en: In no way, then, must it be thought likely,

latin: undique cum vorsum spatium vacet infinitum
en: since space lies empty, infinite, in every direction,

latin: seminaque innumero numero summaque profunda
en: and seeds in numberless number in the deep sum

latin: multimodis volitent aeterno percita motu,
en: fly about in many ways, driven by eternal motion,

latin: hunc unum terrarum orbem caelumque creatum,
en: that this one orb of lands and this sky alone were created,

latin: nil agere illa foris tot corpora materiai;
en: and those so many bodies of matter outside do nothing;

latin: cum praesertim hic sit natura factus et ipsa
en: especially since this world was made by nature, and the seeds

latin: sponte sua forte offensando semina rerum
en: of things themselves, of their own accord, colliding by chance,

latin: multimodis temere in cassum frustraque coacta
en: driven together in many ways, at random, vainly, to no purpose,

latin: tandem coluerunt ea quae coniecta repente
en: at last grew together into those which, suddenly thrown together,

latin: magnarum rerum fierent exordia semper,
en: might become forever the origins of great things,

latin: terrai maris et caeli generisque animantum.
en: of earth and sea and sky and the race of living things.

latin: quare etiam atque etiam talis fateare necesse est
en: Therefore again and again you must confess

latin: esse alios alibi congressus materiai,
en: that there are elsewhere other gatherings of matter

latin: qualis hic est, avido complexu quem tenet aether.
en: such as this is, which the ether holds in its greedy embrace.

latin: Praeterea cum materies est multa parata,
en: Further, when much matter is made ready,

latin: cum locus est praesto nec res nec causa moratur
en: when place is at hand and no thing and no cause

latin: ulla, geri debent ni mirum et confieri res.
en: delays, things must surely be carried on and come to be.

latin: nunc et seminibus si tanta est copia, quantam
en: As it is, if there is such a store of seeds as

latin: enumerare aetas animantum non queat omnis,
en: the whole life of living things could not count out,

latin: quis eadem natura manet, quae semina rerum
en: and the same nature remains, which can throw the seeds of things

latin: conicere in loca quaeque queat simili ratione
en: together into every place in the same way

latin: atque huc sunt coniecta, necesse est confiteare
en: as they have been thrown together here, you must confess

latin: esse alios aliis terrarum in partibus orbis
en: that in other regions there are other orbs of lands

latin: et varias hominum gentis et saecla ferarum.
en: and various races of men and generations of wild beasts.

latin: Huc accedit ut in summa res nulla sit una,
en: Add to this that in the sum there is no one thing

latin: unica quae gignatur et unica solaque crescat,
en: that is born unique and grows unique and alone,

latin: quin aliquoius siet saecli permultaque eodem
en: but is of some generation, and very many are of the same

latin: sint genere. in primis animalibus indice mente
en: kind. First, among living creatures, with your mind as guide,

latin: invenies sic montivagum genus esse ferarum,
en: you will find it so with the mountain-roaming race of wild beasts,

latin: sic hominum geminam prolem, sic denique mutas
en: so with the twin offspring of men, so finally with the mute

latin: squamigerum pecudes et corpora cuncta volantum.
en: herds of the scaly ones and all the bodies of flying things.

latin: qua propter caelum simili ratione fatendumst
en: Therefore you must confess, on a like principle, that sky

latin: terramque et solem, lunam mare cetera quae sunt,
en: and earth and sun, moon, sea, and all else that is,

latin: non esse unica, sed numero magis innumerali;
en: are not unique, but rather of number beyond numbering;

latin: quando quidem vitae depactus terminus alte
en: since the boundary-stone of life, set deep,

latin: tam manet haec et tam nativo corpore constant
en: awaits these as surely, and they are of a body as born

latin: quam genus omne, quod his generatimst rebus abundans.
en: as every kind that abounds here, kind by kind, in such things.

latin: Quae bene cognita si teneas, natura videtur
en: If you know these things well and hold them, nature is seen

latin: libera continuo, dominis privata superbis,
en: to be free at once, stripped of proud masters,

latin: ipsa sua per se sponte omnia dis agere expers.
en: doing all things of herself, by her own accord, without the gods.

latin: nam pro sancta deum tranquilla pectora pace
en: For by the holy hearts of the gods, which in tranquil peace

latin: quae placidum degunt aevom vitamque serenam,
en: pass a placid age and a serene life,

latin: quis regere immensi summam, quis habere profundi
en: who can rule the sum of the immeasurable, who hold in hand

latin: indu manu validas potis est moderanter habenas,
en: the strong reins of the deep and guide them,

latin: quis pariter caelos omnis convertere et omnis
en: who can turn all the heavens alike, and warm

latin: ignibus aetheriis terras suffire feracis,
en: all the fruitful lands with fires of the ether,

latin: omnibus inve locis esse omni tempore praesto,
en: or be present in all places at all times,

latin: nubibus ut tenebras faciat caelique serena
en: to make darkness with clouds and shake the calm of heaven

latin: concutiat sonitu, tum fulmina mittat et aedis
en: with sound, then hurl thunderbolts, and often

latin: saepe suas disturbet et in deserta recedens
en: throw down his own shrines, and, withdrawing into deserts,

latin: saeviat exercens telum, quod saepe nocentes
en: rage there, exercising his bolt, which often passes the guilty

latin: praeterit exanimatque indignos inque merentes?
en: by, and strikes dead the unworthy and the undeserving?

latin: Multaque post mundi tempus genitale diemque
en: And many bodies, after the birth-time of the world

latin: primigenum maris et terrae solisque coortum
en: and the first-born day of sea and earth and the rising of the sun,

latin: addita corpora sunt extrinsecus, addita circum
en: were added from outside, and added round about

latin: semina, quae magnum iaculando contulit omne,
en: were seeds, which the great whole brought together by hurling them,

latin: unde mare et terrae possent augescere et unde
en: from which the sea and the lands could increase, and from which

latin: appareret spatium caeli domus altaque tecta
en: heaven's house could show its room, and lift its lofty roof

latin: tolleret a terris procul et consurgeret aer.
en: far from the lands, and the air rise up.

latin: nam sua cuique, locis ex omnibus, omnia plagis
en: For each to its own, from every place, all bodies by blows

latin: corpora distribuuntur et ad sua saecla recedunt,
en: are distributed, and go back to their own kinds:

latin: umor ad umorem, terreno corpore terra
en: moisture to moisture; earth grows from earthy body,

latin: crescit et ignem ignes procudunt aetheraque aether,
en: and fires forge fire, and ether forges ether,

latin: donique ad extremum crescendi perfica finem
en: until to the farthest limit of growth, bringing all to completion,

latin: omnia perduxit rerum natura creatrix;
en: the creating nature of things has led all things on;

latin: ut fit ubi nihilo iam plus est quod datur intra
en: as happens when nothing more is now given within

latin: vitalis venas quam quod fluit atque recedit.
en: the vital veins than flows away and withdraws.

latin: omnibus hic aetas debet consistere rebus,
en: Here the age of all things must come to a stand,

latin: hic natura suis refrenat viribus auctum.
en: here nature reins in growth with her own strength.

latin: nam quae cumque vides hilaro grandescere adauctu
en: For whatever things you see grow big with cheerful increase

latin: paulatimque gradus aetatis scandere adultae,
en: and little by little climb the steps of grown age

latin: plura sibi adsumunt quam de se corpora mittunt,
en: take more bodies into themselves than they send out from themselves,

latin: dum facile in venas cibus omnis inditur et dum
en: while all the food is easily put into their veins, and while

latin: non ita sunt late dispessa, ut multa remittant
en: they are not spread so widely that they give back much

latin: et plus dispendi faciant quam vescitur aetas.
en: and make more waste than their age feeds upon.

latin: nam certe fluere atque recedere corpora rebus
en: For certainly we must grant that many bodies flow

latin: multa manus dandum est; sed plura accedere debent,
en: and withdraw from things; but more must come in,

latin: donec alescendi summum tetigere cacumen.
en: until they have touched the topmost peak of growing.

latin: inde minutatim vires et robur adultum
en: From then, little by little, age breaks the strength

latin: frangit et in partem peiorem liquitur aetas.
en: and grown vigor, and melts away into the worse part.

latin: quippe etenim quanto est res amplior, augmine adempto,
en: For indeed, the larger a thing is, once its increase is taken away,

latin: et quo latior est, in cunctas undique partis
en: and the wider it is, into all directions on every side

latin: plura modo dispargit et a se corpora mittit,
en: the more bodies it scatters now and sends out from itself,

latin: nec facile in venas cibus omnis diditur ei
en: nor is all the food easily distributed into its veins,

latin: nec satis est, pro quam largos exaestuat aestus,
en: nor is there enough, for the lavish tides it pours out,

latin: unde queat tantum suboriri ac subpeditare.
en: from which as much could arise again and be supplied.

latin: iure igitur pereunt, cum rarefacta fluendo
en: Rightly, therefore, they perish, when they have grown rare

latin: sunt et cum externis succumbunt omnia plagis,
en: by flowing, and all things give way beneath blows from outside,

latin: quando quidem grandi cibus aevo denique defit,
en: since in great age food at last runs short,

latin: nec tuditantia rem cessant extrinsecus ullam
en: and the bodies battering from outside never cease

latin: corpora conficere et plagis infesta domare.
en: to wear a thing down and subdue it with hostile blows.

latin: Sic igitur magni quoque circum moenia mundi
en: So therefore the walls of the great world round about

latin: expugnata dabunt labem putrisque ruinas;
en: will also be stormed, and give way to decay and crumbling ruin;

latin: omnia debet enim cibus integrare novando
en: for food must make all things whole by renewing them,

latin: et fulcire cibus, cibus omnia sustentare,
en: food must prop them up, food must sustain all things,

latin: ne quiquam, quoniam nec venae perpetiuntur
en: in vain, since neither do the veins endure to take in

latin: quod satis est, neque quantum opus est natura ministrat.
en: what is enough, nor does nature supply as much as is needed.

latin: Iamque adeo fracta est aetas effetaque tellus
en: And indeed even now the age is broken, and the worn-out earth

latin: vix animalia parva creat, quae cuncta creavit
en: scarcely creates small animals, she who created all

latin: saecla deditque ferarum ingentia corpora partu.
en: kinds, and gave birth to the huge bodies of wild beasts.

latin: haud, ut opinor, enim mortalia saecla superne
en: For it was not, I think, that the mortal kinds from on high

latin: aurea de caelo demisit funis in arva
en: a golden rope let down from heaven into the fields,

latin: nec mare nec fluctus plangentis saxa crearunt,
en: nor did the sea and the waves beating on the rocks create them,

latin: sed genuit tellus eadem quae nunc alit ex se.
en: but the earth bore them, the same that now feeds them from herself.

latin: praeterea nitidas fruges vinetaque laeta
en: Further, the shining crops and the glad vineyards

latin: sponte sua primum mortalibus ipsa creavit,
en: she herself, of her own accord, first created for mortals,

latin: ipsa dedit dulcis fetus et pabula laeta;
en: she herself gave sweet fruits and glad pastures;

latin: quae nunc vix nostro grandescunt aucta labore,
en: which now scarcely grow great, increased by our labor,

latin: conterimusque boves et viris agricolarum,
en: and we wear out the oxen and the strength of the farmers,

latin: conficimus ferrum vix arvis suppeditati:
en: we wear down the iron, we whom the fields scarcely supply:

latin: usque adeo parcunt fetus augentque laborem.
en: so much do they stint their fruits and increase the labor.

latin: iamque caput quassans grandis suspirat arator
en: And now the aged plowman shakes his head and sighs

latin: crebrius, in cassum magnos cecidisse labores,
en: more often that his great labors have come to nothing,

latin: et cum tempora temporibus praesentia confert
en: and when he compares the present times with times

latin: praeteritis, laudat fortunas saepe parentis.
en: gone by, he often praises his father's fortunes.

latin: tristis item vetulae vitis sator atque vietae
en: Gloomily too the planter of the old and shriveled vine

latin: temporis incusat momen saeclumque fatigat,
en: blames the drift of time and wearies the age with complaint,

latin: et crepat, antiquum genus ut pietate repletum
en: and grumbles how the race of old, filled with piety,

latin: perfacile angustis tolerarit finibus aevom,
en: bore life very easily within narrow bounds,

latin: cum minor esset agri multo modus ante viritim;
en: though the measure of land for each man was far smaller before;

latin: nec tenet omnia paulatim tabescere et ire
en: nor does he grasp that all things waste away by degrees and go

latin: ad capulum spatio aetatis defessa vetusto.
en: to the bier, worn out by the ancient span of age.
